walkthroughs.body_html:
Problem Solving & Programming — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Problem Solving & Programming brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Problem Solving & Programming.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The three fundamental programming constructs are:
options: Sequence, selection and iteration
Input, output and storage
Compile, link and run
Stacks, queues and trees

mcqs.q: Every recursive subroutine must have a base case because otherwise it would:
options: Run faster than intended
Call itself indefinitely until the call stack overflows
Sort its data incorrectly
Convert itself into iteration

mcqs.q: A local variable declared inside a function can be accessed:
options: Only within that function
From anywhere in the program
Only by the operating system
Only after the program ends

mcqs.q: Which computational method repeatedly halves a problem, solves the parts, and combines the results?
options: Backtracking
Brute force
Divide and conquer
Caching

mcqs.q: Is recursion just another name for a loop?
options: Yes - recursion is a loop that runs backwards.
Yes - the compiler treats recursion and loops as identical.
Yes - local variables are slower so globals should be preferred.
No - recursion solves a problem through self-calls that each add a stack frame, while iteration repeats within one frame; they can compute the same things but work differently.

mcqs.q: Are global variables good practice because every subroutine can reach them?
options: Yes - selection and iteration are the same construct.
Yes - using globals everywhere makes programs simpler and safer.
Yes - local variables are slower so globals should be preferred.
No - that universal reach is the danger: any part of the program can change them, creating hidden dependencies and bugs; passing parameters keeps interfaces explicit.

mcqs.q: Is an IF statement a form of iteration?
options: No - IF is selection: it chooses between paths once; iteration constructs such as WHILE and FOR repeat statements multiple times.
Yes - IF repeats its block until the condition becomes false.
Yes - recursion is a loop that runs backwards.
Yes - selection and iteration are the same construct.
